RadioReach vs Groover

By the RadioReach editorial team Published August 19, 2026 Reviewed August 19, 2026

Groover is a per-submission platform with a guaranteed response from curators, labels, journalists and some radio stations. RadioReach is a one-time file of radio contacts you pitch yourself. Groover suits artists who want a reply and a broad industry net; RadioReach suits artists running a self-directed radio campaign who want unlimited reuse for a fixed cost.

  • Side by side
  • Groover, from its own site

Who wrote this: RadioReach — we sell one of the products compared here. We have tried to describe the alternatives accurately and to say plainly where they are the better purchase. Competitor facts come from their own websites with access dates; where we could not verify a figure from a primary source, we say so instead of repeating it. Fact-checked 2026-08-18.

The core difference

Groover's distinguishing feature is breadth of contact type. Alongside playlist curators it lists labels, media outlets, journalists, bookers and radio stations, which makes it a general music-industry outreach tool rather than a playlist-only one. It also guarantees that whoever you send to will respond.

RadioReach is narrower on purpose. It covers one channel — radio — and gives you the contacts rather than a route through a platform. Nobody is obliged to reply to you. In exchange, the cost does not scale with the number of stations you contact or the number of releases you promote.

Groover listing radio stations among its contact types is the genuine overlap with what we sell, and it is worth being straight about: if you want to reach a handful of radio stations and would rather have a guaranteed reply than a bigger list, that is a reasonable argument for using Groover instead of us.

Best for / avoid when

Groover is the better buy when

  • You want guaranteed responses rather than silence.
  • You are targeting Europe, where its curator base is strong.
  • You want one tool covering blogs, labels, playlists and radio together.

Avoid Groover when

  • Your budget cannot absorb a recurring per-submission cost each release.
  • You want a large radio list to work through systematically.
  • You want direct inbox relationships rather than platform-mediated ones.

RadioReach is the better buy when

  • Radio is the channel and the United States is the market.
  • You want a fixed cost and unlimited reuse.
  • You would rather write a genuinely personal pitch than a templated one.

Avoid RadioReach when

  • You need a reply, or feedback, or any form of guarantee.
  • Your campaign is primarily European.
  • You want playlist and press coverage in the same motion.

Limitations of this page

Groover's pricing page did not resolve at the fact-check date, so credit costs are not quoted here. The attributes above are drawn from Groover's public homepage and are its own description of its service. We have not run a controlled campaign through Groover, so nothing here should be read as an outcome comparison.

Frequently asked questions

Does Groover include radio stations?

Yes. Groover's own site lists radio stations among its contact types alongside curators, labels and journalists. If you want a small number of radio contacts with a guaranteed response, that is a real alternative to buying a contact file — the trade-off is cost per submission versus list size.
